title: Orders home: choose the layout
question: The Bahn world is fixed (birch ground, asphalt ink, sand panels, pill controls, wide uppercase display). Pick how the Orders home is organised.

options.label: Stage rail
options.lineage: Bahn's route line, orange pickup pin to red delivery pin
options.thesis: The order lifecycle drawn as one route line; pick a stop to see its orders.
options.viewport: Top bar with pill nav. A full-width rail of seven stages with big counts, then a dense list of the chosen stage, rows needing a person first.
options.risk: Only one stage is visible at a time, so a cross-stage scan takes clicks.

options.label: One table
options.lineage: Bahn's sand panels and segmented track
options.thesis: All 100 orders in one sortable table, filtered by stage pills and a 'needs a person' switch.
options.viewport: Top bar, title row with search, a segmented stage filter, then a full-width table: car, reference, customer, route, stage, decisive date, why it needs a person.
options.risk: The densest option; at projector distance rows read small.

options.label: Queue and preview
options.lineage: Bahn's large rounded cards over a birch ground
options.thesis: A ranked queue of what needs a person on the left; the selected order opens beside it.
options.viewport: Top bar, stage counts as pills, a queue column of orders needing a person, and a large preview panel with the car, route and open items.
options.risk: Quiet orders are out of sight; reaching them means switching the queue filter.
